submitted.rationale: Index 30 (Ni 0.17, Sb 0.83) had the highest EQE of the three measured: 1.91%, compared with 0.012% for index 21 and 0.0007% for index 27. XRD at indices 21 and 30 shows similar trirutile-like patterns. Neither MACE nor MEGNet explained the performance, since the MEGNet band gaps were not usable. The Ni-rich half of the library (indices 0–20) was never measured.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE 0.012%, at the NiSb2O6 stoichiometry
Measured EQE 0.0007%, so the high EQE is confined to the Sb-rich edge
Not measured, budget ran out. They are expected to be dominated by NiO (usually p-type), so not favoured for a photoanode, but this was never tested

consultations.verdict: Support (weak): MACE puts trirutile NiSb2O6 on the hull, so index 21 (Sb 0.66, right at the NiSb2O6 stoichiometry) should be close to single-phase. The MEGNet HSE gap of 0.04 eV is implausibly low for a Ni2+ antimonate and is probably an artifact of how the model treats open-shell Ni, so I am not using it.

Uninformative for index 30: MACE puts Ni2Sb2O7 0.27 eV/atom above the hull, so the Ni:Sb 1:1 pyrochlore is unlikely to form. The films should be NiSb2O6 plus Ni oxide or Sb oxide, and the XRD of index 30 looks like index 21's. I am measuring index 30 to sample the Sb-rich end of the composition line.

Uninformative: MEGNet predicts a 3.6 eV gap for the NiSb2O4 cell (mp-21275), which is above the 2.1 eV photon energy and so says nothing about which composition absorbs better. The measurements do give a lead: EQE rose sharply from Sb 0.66 (0.012%) to Sb 0.83 (1.9%), so the optimum is Sb-rich. I am measuring index 27 (Sb 0.79) to check for a maximum inside the Sb-rich region, not at its edge.
